advisory.finding: The three isolation regression tests have no negative control proving the guard actually FAILS when a node leaks into the ambient store. Combined with the coarse snapshot, a guard that can never trip is indistinguishable from real isolation, so the tests may pass regardless of whether the isolation fix is effective.

ABSENCE: no recursive file-level snapshot (e.g. `git status --porcelain` on the tracker, or a recursive rglob of files) that would catch an uncommitted file write into an existing directory.
dropped.finding: The store-isolation guard's post-run snapshot compares only top-level DIRECTORY NAMES (`{path.name for path in tracker.iterdir() if path.is_dir()}`) and the committed HEAD; it ignores files and nested content. A synthetic sidecar leaked as a FILE at the tracker root (or into a pre-existing subdir) WITHOUT a commit would leave both the HEAD and the dir-name set unchanged, so the guard cannot detect the exact 'synthetic T-1 / rec-0000 sidecar' leak the change targets.
dropped.suggested_fix: Replace the dir-name-set comparison with a recursive file snapshot and/or add a `git status --porcelain` (untracked-included) assertion on the tracker so uncommitted file writes into existing directories are caught.
